teaser.en: In the wet valleys below the Shimba Hills grows a wild relative of the palm that fills supermarket shelves worldwide with oil.

summary.en: *Mtsikitsi*, the wild oil palm, is a feather palm of wet valley bottoms and stream sides on the south coast. Its orange-red fruits give palm oil, and it is also tapped for palm wine.

about.en:
*Mtsikitsi* is a single-stemmed feather palm. The trunk is rough with the stubs of old leaf bases, and the leaf stalks are spiny. The crown holds long, arching fronds.

The fruits grow in dense, heavy bunches tucked among the leaf bases. Each fruit is small and plum-shaped, ripening to orange-red, with an oily pulp around a hard kernel.

where.en: It grows in wet valley bottoms and along streams on the south coast, such as at the foot of the Shimba Hills and around Msambweni. Look for its feathery crown above the green of a valley floor.

uses.en: Oil is pressed from the fruit. The palm is also tapped for palm wine, and its leaves are used.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name *mtsikitsi* and describes it as the 'wild oil palm'. The Mgombato dictionary also gives *mtsikitsi* for the wild or Guinea oil palm, and notes that the same word is used for cycads. Pakia uses *mtsikitsi* for the raffia palm too, so the name covers more than one plant. In Swahili it is *mchikichi* (Mgombato adds *mchikichi wa bara*) or *mwese*. In English it is the oil palm, and its scientific name is *Elaeis guineensis*.

reason.en: The raffia palm, which shares the name mtsikitsi
A cycad: Mgombato says mtsikitsi is also used for cycads
Another palm tapped for palm wine
Another palm of wet valleys and stream banks

mgombato: mtsikitsi (mi) type of plant: wild oil palm, Guinea oil palm (Elaeis guineensis); also used of cycads; mchikichi (wa bara), miwese.
sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
